subject: PIT histograms - choosing between candidate models

messages.author: e498b38f01df2491
messages.subject: PIT histograms - choosing between candidate models
parts:
Dear,

I have estimated density of whales through the besag function via inla. Covariates were used in the models and I would like to compare and choose the best fit between the candidate models.

The five models are indistinguishable by the DICs (314.15, 314.26, 314.37, 314.7, 315.89). Therefore, I would like to know if I can use PIT histograms for choosing the model for inference. I was thinking about analyze which model has the PIT histogram most similar to a uniform distribution.

So, my questions are:
- Can I choose between models at this manner?
- How can I formally compare such histograms?

The histograms could be seen here (Dropbox link): https://www.dropbox.com/sh/d17ituj7f7dfk3a/AAC9Drimp9KLg44rP2bhs3Cia?dl=0

Thank you in advance.

Regards,
Heloise

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] PIT histograms - choosing between candidate models
parts:
Distinguishing between those models will be difficult regardless of comparison method, but there is an example in the help text for inla.ks.plot for comparing the PIT values to uniforms, based on Kolmogorov-Smirnov, so take a look at
  ?inla.ks.plot

Finn

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] PIT histograms - choosing between candidate models
parts: In this case, should I choose the higher p-value model (model 3)? It is justifiable to choose a model between p-values between 0.05 and 0.12?

Just as the DIC values were nearly indistinguishable, so are the KS-tests...
One could argue for choosing a model that does well on both methods, which in this case is model 3 (model 5 did well for DIC but not for K-S).

But as you indicate, 0.12 on K-S is not necessarily "good" in absolute terms, so the results cannot be used to confidently say that model 3 is "good", just that it appears to do better than the other models you have.

Finn

Regards,
Heloise
